clue.text: Ship in for repairs detailed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: brought into a dock, as a vessel is for repairs
second meaning, read as de-tailed: with the tail cut short, as with some dog breeds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'thorough', but read it as de-tailed: having had its tail cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel berthed at a harbour quay has been put in, and an animal whose tail has been cut short has been treated the same way in name.

clue.text: Boy in gambling game gets nowhere near

definitions.note: the answer is a noun: a far-off place, one nowhere near

indicators.note: one thing set in another means the boy's name sits inside the game's name

parts.note: dice is a game played for stakes
a boy's name, short for Stanley

explanation.surface: A lad who takes up dice playing ends up going nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets nowhere near' reads as failing; the definition is the noun for a remote place, as in 'in the distance'.
explanation.definitionFit: The distance is a remote spot far away, a place that lies nowhere close at hand.

clue.text: Room with bunks and French furniture

parts.note: a ship's cabin is a small room fitted with bunks
French for 'and', standing in for the clue's 'and'

explanation.surface: A bedroom with bunk beds plus some furnishings from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and French' means the French for 'and', which is ET.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet is a cupboard with shelves or drawers, a standard piece of household furnishing.

clue.text: Capital sort of rock

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the capital city of Scotland
second meaning: a crumbly stick of sugar confectionery named after that city

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests geology (the city's castle does stand on one), but here it is British rock, a hard stick of boiled sugar sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Edinburgh is Scotland's capital city, and Edinburgh rock is a traditional pastel-coloured sugar sweet made there.

clue.text: Unfinished year book ?

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its ending, so the closing letters are cut away

parts.note: an old word for a year, twelve months

explanation.surface: A calendar year left incomplete, about which a book was written.
explanation.walkthrough: TWELVEMONTH loses its last three letters, NTH, to leave TWELVEMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelvemo is a book size, also written 12mo, where each printed sheet is folded into twelve leaves.

clue.text: Celebration where "we three" (et al) would meet again

definitions.text: Celebration where "we three" (et al) would meet again

parts.words: Celebration where "we three" (et al) would meet again
parts.note: surface reading: a reunion party for some trio and friends
setter's reading: the three weird sisters of Macbeth, who open the play asking when they shall meet again, and their kind gathering at midnight

explanation.surface: A reunion party where an old trio and their friends gather once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth opens with the three witches asking 'When shall we three meet again?'; a midnight gathering of witches is a witches' sabbath.
explanation.definitionFit: A witches' sabbath is the midnight assembly of witches in folklore, a celebration at which the Macbeth trio and others would gather.

clue.text: A sucker for the rest of the players

definitions.text: A sucker for the rest of the players

parts.words: A sucker for the rest of the players
parts.note: surface reading: an easy dupe whom the other card players take money from
setter's reading: a fruit that is sucked, also slang for a dud or a fool

explanation.walkthrough: A sucker sounds like a mark at a card table; it is also a sour citrus fruit you might suck. At the interval of a match, players were traditionally given slices of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon is slang for a dud or a hopeless person, and players sucked lemon segments at half-time.

clue.text: Locally prevalent medicine is mixed without one

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the remaining letters are rearranged
without means lacking, so a letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A drug is being mixed up without a single ingredient, and something is spreading in the area.
explanation.walkthrough: MEDICINE loses one I to give MEDICNE, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An endemic disease is one regularly found among a particular people or region, so it is prevalent in that locality.

clue.text: Handy treatment for 25

parts.note: surface reading: a convenient remedy, or care applied with the hands
setter's reading: 25 is the answer to 25-across, paying someone off, and the idiom is greasing a person's palm

explanation.walkthrough: 'Handy' points at the hand: to grease someone's palm is to bribe them, and 25-across is BRIBERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lubricating someone's palm is an idiom for paying them a bribe, so applying grease to the hand is that corrupt treatment.

clue.text: Do they tone down one's professional credentials ?

definitions.note: a question whose answer is the plural noun: they are things that soften
definitions.meaning: first meaning: limiting conditions added to a statement, softening its force
second meaning: certificates or diplomas showing one is trained for a job

explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as if credentials might make a person modest; in fact the word for reservations that soften a statement is also the word for certificates.
explanation.definitionFit: Qualifications are both reservations that limit a claim and the certificates proving fitness for a trade or career.

clue.text: Rob's quite put out by his nickname

indicators.note: put out means upset or disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Robert is rather annoyed by what people call him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as 'annoyed', but it is telling you to rearrange the nine letters of Rob's quite.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobriquet is an assumed name or epithet given to a person, the same thing as a familiar nickname.

clue.text: Interfere, say, in an award

indicators.note: say means spoken out loud, so the word is what the sound gives, not its spelling

parts.note: to meddle is to interfere, and it is pronounced the same as the prize word

explanation.surface: Someone interfering in the decision over who wins a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A medal is a metal disc given as a prize or honour for achievement, so it is a kind of award.

clue.text: She'd be in the record

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the little verb goes within the word for a record

parts.note: an annal is the record of a single year's events
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman who would like to appear in the history books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' alone is the definition, asking for a woman's name; annals, usually plural, are yearly chronicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Annabel is a woman's first name, so it stands for an unnamed female person, the pronoun she.

clue.text: Tyburn operative taking up modern gliding ?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Tyburn was London's chief place of public execution, so its worker was the executioner at the gallows
second meaning, whimsically: a fellow who takes up hang-gliding, the newly fashionable sport of the time

explanation.walkthrough: Tyburn, near today's Marble Arch, was London's gallows site for centuries. The second half splits the answer into a sport and a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: An executioner at the gallows was the hangman, and a person who hang-glides could jokingly be called a hang man.

clue.text: Provide for such a cousin

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to supply food or what is needed

definitions.note: names the first half of the old compound cater-cousin
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a ...-cousin is an old word, used by Shakespeare, for an intimate friend

explanation.walkthrough: 'Provide for' looks like the whole definition, but 'for' only joins the two halves; the second half needs the archaic cater-cousin.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply food or what is wanted, and a cater-cousin is an archaic term for a close companion.

clue.text: Dashing fellow making easy money

parts.note: dashing means moving quickly
a buck is a lively young man

explanation.surface: A stylish young man who earns money without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashing fellow' reads as one dashing man, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast buck is a sum earned quickly and with little effort, often dishonestly, so it is effortless cash.

clue.text: Block arrangement for a bird race

indicators.note: an arrangement is a putting in order, so the letters are laid out anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Making the setup for a pigeon race or similar contest of birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A barricade is an improvised barrier across a street or entrance, something that obstructs passage.

clue.text: Rosalind as wine-waiter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the name Rosalind takes when disguised as a boy in Shakespeare's As You Like It
second meaning: the Trojan youth carried off to be cupbearer to the gods on Olympus

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rosalind as wine-waiter' sounds like a casting note; it is two separate meanings, one from Shakespeare and one from Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In As You Like It, Rosalind calls herself Ganymede when in disguise, and the mythical Ganymede poured drink for Zeus.

clue.text: Spanish dance not to be sneezed at; however!

parts.note: surface reading: a lively dance from Spain

parts.words: not to be sneezed at; however!
parts.note: setter's reading: the name, said aloud, is full of sneezing noises, like a-choo, yet it is no sneeze

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not to be sneezed at' is the idiom for something worth having; here it jokes that the dance's name sounds like a string of sneezes.
explanation.definitionFit: The cachucha is a lively Andalusian solo dance in triple time, performed with castanets, from southern Spain.

clue.text: The silly old man's nuts!

indicators.note: silly means foolish and muddled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that the foolish elderly fellow has gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like a verdict on the old man's sanity; it is the definition, in its literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Almonds are the edible kernels of the almond tree's fruit, a familiar kind of tree nut.

clue.text: Girl artist carries the bricks

indicators.note: carries means holds, so the artist's letters hold the other piece inside them

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
a hod is the trough on a pole used to carry bricks

explanation.surface: A young woman painter who lugs bricks around.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, for Royal Academician, is the crossword's standard artist. The hod is named by what it carries.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda is a female first name, so it is one example of what the clue calls a girl.

clue.text: Old boy observing instructions

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
eyeing, here spelt without the second E, means watching

explanation.walkthrough: 'Observing' does double duty: watching for the wordplay, complying in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeying means complying with orders, the same as abiding by or keeping to commands that have been given.

clue.text: Expels from eg 23 in an emergency

definitions.note: an elliptical phrase: gets out of a 23 in a crisis
definitions.meaning: second meaning: what a pilot does from 23-across, an aircraft, when it is about to crash

explanation.walkthrough: 23-across is JUMP JET; a pilot in trouble leaves such an aircraft by the ejector seat.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject is to throw something out forcibly, and a pilot ejects by firing the escape seat out of the cockpit.

clue.text: Its main feature shown in elevation in perpendicular plane

definitions.text: Its main feature shown in elevation in perpendicular plane

parts.words: Its main feature shown in elevation in perpendicular plane
parts.note: surface reading: a technical drawing, showing something's chief feature in an elevation drawn on a vertical plane
setter's reading: an aircraft that rises straight upwards, its key feature being vertical take-off

explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevation' and 'plane' sound like draughtsman's geometry, but the plane is an aircraft and elevation is going up.
explanation.definitionFit: A jump jet, such as the Harrier, is a fighter aircraft able to take off and land vertically without a runway.

clue.text: Girl novelist ?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a woman's first name
second meaning: the Irish writer of Ulysses

explanation.definitionFit: Joyce is a female first name, and James Joyce was the Irish author of Ulysses and Finnegans Wake.

clue.text: By which a number may be squared

definitions.text: By which a number may be squared

parts.words: By which a number may be squared
parts.note: surface reading: arithmetic, multiplying a figure by itself
setter's reading: a number of people may be squared, meaning paid off to keep them quiet

explanation.walkthrough: 'Squared' looks mathematical, but to square someone is slang for buying their silence or cooperation.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying people off corruptly, which is to square them in slang, is the offence of offering illicit payments.

clue.text: Appearing sweet in lilac and yellow stripes?

indicators.note: appearing in means showing up inside the following words, which contain the answer

parts.note: the letters run across the end of lilac, all of and, and the start of yellow
surface padding: bands of alternating colour, which completes the picture of a striped sweet

explanation.surface: A confection decorated with mauve and yellow stripes.
explanation.walkthrough: Candy stripes are alternating bands of colour, which makes the surface fit the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Candy is the American word for sweets or confectionery, and in Britain it means sugar sweets such as rock.

clue.text: New craze is to give some-pile a big send-off

definitions.note: the scan garbles 'someone' as some-pile; the printed definition is 'give someone a big send-off'

indicators.note: new means made fresh, so the following letters are reformed into a different word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The latest fad is to throw a lavish farewell party for somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: A big send-off sounds like a party; here it means being sent away for good, as in the Athenian vote banishing a citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: To ostracize is to exclude a person from society, in effect banishing them, which is sending them off in a hostile way.

clue.text: Sort of account for 13's customers?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bookkeeping account where uncertain items are held until they can be placed properly

definitions.note: the answer is what those customers are in, not the customers themselves
definitions.meaning: second meaning: 13-across is HANGMAN, whose customers are left hanging, in a state of anxious uncertainty

explanation.walkthrough: A suspense account is accounting jargon; the hangman's clients are literally suspended, a grim pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspense account holds unallocated sums temporarily, and those on the gallows are literally suspended, also anxiously uncertain.

clue.text: Bird decapitated this hound

parts.note: surface reading: a bird of prey killed and beheaded a hunting dog
setter's reading: reversed logic, the bird of prey is what this hound becomes once its first letter is cut off

explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay runs backwards: remove the head, the first letter B, from the dog and you get EAGLE, the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The beagle is a small short-legged scent hound bred for tracking hares, so it is a breed of hunting dog.
